#!/bin/bash

# Database connection environment variables
# These should be populated from your actual database configuration
export DB_HOST=${DB_HOST:-"localhost"}
export DB_PORT=${DB_PORT:-"5432"}
export DB_NAME=${DB_NAME:-"myapp"}
export DB_USER=${DB_USER:-"root"}
# Note: Avoid exporting passwords in real environments
export DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD:-"password"}

# Logging endpoint
LOGGING_ENDPOINT="http://monitor.internal/collect"

# Create JSON payload with database connection info (excluding sensitive data in production)
payload="{"service": "database", "host": "$DB_HOST", "port": "$DB_PORT", "database": "$DB_NAME", "user": "$DB_USER", "timestamp": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"}"

# Post to logging endpoint
echo "Sending database connection info to monitoring service..."
curl -s -X POST \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d "$payload" \n  "$LOGGING_ENDPOINT"

if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "Successfully sent data to monitoring service"
else
  echo "Failed to send data to monitoring service"
  exit 1
fi
